classification.habitat: Warm humid tropical forests and plantations; trained on support trees in areas of high rainfall.
classification.distribution: Native to the Western Ghats; cultivated in Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Konkan and parts of North-East India.

identification.description: Small globose, dark brown to black, reticulately wrinkled dried fruits with pungent aromatic taste.
identification.whole_plant: Perennial woody climber climbing by adventitious roots at the nodes, with jointed stems and pendulous fruiting spikes.
identification.root: Adventitious clinging roots arise at the swollen nodes; underground roots fibrous.
identification.stem: Stout, jointed, woody climbing stem, swollen at the nodes.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate, broadly ovate, acuminate, leathery, dark green and glossy, with 5–7 prominent curved veins.
identification.flower: Minute flowers on pendulous spikes 3–15 cm long, opposite the leaves.
identification.fruit: Fruits greyish-black to black, hard, wrinkled, 0.4–0.5 cm in diameter; odour aromatic, taste pungent.
identification.seed: Single seed per berry, globose, with a white starchy perisperm (white pepper is the seed freed from the pericarp).
identification_points: Globose black fruit, 4–5 mm in diameter
Aromatic odour and sharply pungent taste

therapeutics.anupana: Madhu (honey) in Kasa and Pratishyaya, as with Trikatu
therapeutics.precautions: Ushna and Tikshna; it is Pittakara and may cause burning in the stomach or throat with excess use. Use within the stated dose.
therapeutics.contraindications: Amlapitta, peptic ulcer, Raktapitta and other Pitta-predominant states; caution in pregnancy in medicinal doses. Piperine can raise blood levels of several medicines.

shlokas:
मरिचं कटुकं तीक्ष्णं दीपनं कफवातजित् ।
उष्णं पित्तकरं रूक्षं श्वासशूलकृमीन् हरेत् ॥६०॥
nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Haritakyadi Varga, verses 59–61; verse 59 gives synonyms and verses 60–61 properties/ardraka comparison. Independently searchable recension; edition numbering may vary.
samhita_references: Ashtanga Hridaya, Sutrasthana 6/161–162 describes Maricha and Pippali
reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

major_constituents: Essential oil (sabinene, limonene, beta-caryophyllene, alpha- and beta-pinene)
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: API lists the alkaloids piperine, chavicine, piperidine and piperettine with essential oil; piperine gives pungency and acts as a bioavailability enhancer.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Black pepper enhances digestion, stimulates metabolism, and helps clear congestion. It is a part of the Trikatu formula.
recognized_uses: Carminative and expectorant in traditional systems
modern_information.safety_notes: Safe in culinary amounts; concentrated piperine may alter the metabolism of drugs such as phenytoin, theophylline and rifampicin.
